note: Oral H4R antagonists went into AD on mouse histamine-itch and Th2-dermatitis models and a human histamine-itch challenge; JNJ-39758979 missed EASI and was stopped by agranulocytosis no tox species had shown, adriforant missed its itch primary in the 2a and every dose in the 2b.
label: Atopic eczema (H4R)

engagement.judgement: Track opened at Dunford 2007, the first use of a selective H4R antagonist (JNJ 7777120, a sibling of the members) in the scratching model; Bell 2004 (doi:10.1038/sj.bjp.0705754) had implicated H4R in mouse itch with the non-selective H3/H4 antagonist thioperamide. Abstract-level reading.
engagement.model: Mouse histamine-induced scratching, H4R knockout + JNJ 7777120
engagement.note: Histamine-evoked scratching was nearly abolished in H4R-knockout mice and by JNJ 7777120; no human read-out existed yet.
engagement.short: H4 blockade abolishes histamine itch in mice
engagement.quote: Histamine and a selective histamine H4 receptor agonist caused scratching responses in mice, which were almost completely attenuated in histamine H4 receptor knockout mice or by pretreatment with the selective histamine H4 receptor antagonist, JNJ 7777120.

engagement.judgement: Separate track from the scratching model: a different system (hapten-driven Th2 skin inflammation, read as oedema, cytokines and cell influx) carrying a different prediction (anti-inflammatory benefit in AD, not only itch relief). Antagonists were JNJ 7777120 and JNJ 28307474, siblings of the members. Abstract-level reading.
engagement.model: Mouse FITC Th2 dermatitis, H4R antagonists
engagement.note: In FITC-induced Th2 dermatitis two H4R antagonists cut ear oedema, cytokines, mast-cell and eosinophil influx; no patient skin read-out existed.
engagement.short: H4 antagonists cut Th2 dermatitis in mice
engagement.quote: Treatment with two specific H4R antagonists before challenge with FITC led to a significant reduction in ear edema, inflammation, mast cell, and eosinophil infiltration.

engagement.magnitude_basis: AUC of pruritus score 0-10 min after histamine challenge vs placebo
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled). Because of carry-over only treatment period 1 was analysed (n per arm ~8); NCT01068223 has no posted results, so registry_date is null. The model compound was JNJ 7777120; JNJ-39758979's own mouse itch data were not verified, so product_in_model is false.
engagement.judgement: Scored as engagement rather than efficacy: the human read-out (histamine-evoked itch in healthy skin) is the same stimulus and read-out the mouse model used, i.e. in-vivo blockade of a stimulus (readout_tier direct). comparison_stated is false because I could not confirm from the abstract that the paper sets the mouse data beside the human data; the pairing with Dunford 2007 is mine.
engagement.model: Mouse histamine-induced scratching, H4R knockout + JNJ 7777120
engagement.note: A single 600 mg dose of JNJ 39758979 cut histamine-challenge itch in healthy men at 2 and 6 h; wheal and flare were unchanged.
engagement.short: Histamine itch fell in dosed volunteers
engagement.quote: Compared with placebo, the reduction of the AUC of pruritus score was significant for JNJ 39758979 at 2 hours (P = 0.0248) and 6 hours (P = 0.0060), and for cetirizine at 6 hours (P = 0.0417).
engagement.reason: Histamine itch fell in dosed volunteers

engagement.magnitude_basis: dose-dependent inhibition of histamine-induced eosinophil shape change ex vivo; no occupancy figure in the abstract
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (paywalled). The read-out is a blood ex-vivo assay, not a skin biopsy; no skin cytokine or eosinophil read-out was ever reported in dosed AD patients. Phase 1 registry NCT01081821 has no posted results.
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: eosinophil shape change is the canonical H4R cellular response and the model's eosinophil-infiltration read-out rests on it, so it is taken as the model's PD read-out moving in humans (ex-vivo blockade of a stimulus, direct). comparison_stated is true because one paper reports the mouse dermatitis dose-response and the human PD side by side.
engagement.model: Mouse FITC Th2 dermatitis, H4R antagonists
engagement.note: Phase 1 volunteers on JNJ-39758979 showed dose-dependent ex-vivo inhibition of histamine-induced eosinophil shape change, the H4 cellular read-out behind the model's eosinophil data.
engagement.short: Eosinophil H4 response blocked ex vivo in volunteers
engagement.quote: In addition, dose-dependent inhibition of histamine-induced eosinophil shape change was detected, suggesting that the H4R was inhibited in vivo.
engagement.reason: Eosinophil H4 read-out blocked in volunteers

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Europe PMC record; epub 2013-08-09, print December 2013). No H4R-antagonist trial in AD reported a keratinocyte-proliferation or epidermal-thickness read-out in dosed patients (Murata 2015, Werfel 2019, ZEST registry record), so the read-out was never measured in humans.
engagement.judgement: Added on the caller's instruction as the class's only patient-derived ex-vivo system; it has no admissible comparison (MODELS_TASK step 3 would otherwise leave it out), so it opens and stays untested. Filed under engagement because the model's read-out is a cellular PD response (proliferation) that no dosed-human study measured; the paper states a mechanism, not a trial prediction, so efficacy is not opened. prediction_level class: the cells were not used to pick patients. Sibling antagonist, product_in_model false.

NCT01497119 has no posted results.
dose.judgement: Table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': contra derived from efficacy. The agranulocytosis is not counted here (decision 16 counts a harm once; the toxicology never predicted it, so it is scored in safety, not as a dose block). Abandonment was for toxicity, but the primary endpoint had already failed at the top dose.

Not neg: neg needs the model's number against a class_threshold the class's successful drugs cleared, and this class has none (checker rule question 7). Year is Murata's online date (2014-12-09).

efficacy.quote: In conclusion, JNJ 39758979 was effective in inhibiting histamine-induced pruritus in healthy subjects.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: placebo-adjusted change in worst-itch NRS at week 8: -0.35 (95% CI -1.21 to 0.51), P = .249
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus the NCT02424253 results record (posted 2021-05-13): sole primary worst-itch NRS change, EASI a secondary. No histamine-challenge study of adriforant was found, so product_in_model is false. JNJ-39758979's own AD trial (Murata 2015) had an EASI primary, so its nominally positive itch secondaries change no status and sit in patient_trials.
efficacy.judgement: Contra: the only pruritus-primary trial of a member failed. The pairing with Kollmeier 2014 is mine (Werfel does not set the challenge beside the trial); a sibling-drug pairing is allowed by the brief. Histamine-evoked itch in healthy skin is histaminergic and AD itch largely is not, which is the simplest reading of the miss.
efficacy.model: Human histamine-iontophoresis itch challenge in healthy volunteers, JNJ 39758979 600 mg
efficacy.note: Adriforant 30 mg for 8 weeks missed the worst-itch NRS primary (-3.03 vs -2.66 placebo, P = .249): challenge itch did not predict AD itch.
efficacy.quote: There was a 3-point reduction (scale, 1-10) in pruritus with ZPL-3893787, but there was a similar reduction with placebo, resulting in a nonsignificant difference (P = .249).
efficacy.reason: Challenge itch did not predict AD itch

patient_trials.quote: Nominally significant improvements across PRO PCRS, PNRS and SGICP assessments were consistently observed, particularly with JNJ-39758979 300 mg.
Patient-reported pruritus subscores obtained from SCORAD were reduced with ZPL-3893787 compared with placebo at week 8 (nonsignificant).

safety.judgement: Opened at 2010 with Thurmond 2014 as the proxy source: the toxicology package had to precede the Phase 1 start (NCT01081821, February 2010). Abstract-level reading; the abstract is silent on the agranulocytosis that had stopped NCT01497119 in February 2012, two years before it appeared.
safety.note: Six-month rat and nine-month monkey toxicology on JNJ-39758979 found nothing of note, and Phase 1 saw only dose-dependent nausea.
safety.short: Rat and monkey tox: excellent safety profile
safety.quote: Preclinical toxicity studies of up to 6 months in rats and 9 months in monkeys indicated an excellent safety profile, supporting the clinical testing of the compound.

safety.magnitude_basis: 2 serious neutropenia/agranulocytosis cases among ~30 patients on 300 mg vs none in 6-month rat and 9-month monkey studies
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The authors call it 'drug-induced agranulocytosis, likely an off-target effect'; no mechanism was ever published, so whether rat or monkey could have shown it is unresolved: a direct marrow toxicity they could, an idiosyncratic clozapine-type reaction they classically cannot. NCT01497119 has no posted results.
safety.judgement: Scored contra because the model's stated prediction ('excellent safety profile') did not hold at the clinical dose, with the caveat above on species visibility. Context that changes no status: the same 300 mg for 12 weeks in 115 asthma patients (NCT00946569, Kollmeier 2018, doi:10.1111/cea.13154) produced no serious adverse events; adriforant showed no neutropenia in the 2a ('ZPL-3893787 was well tolerated') or across 291 patients in the 2b (no haematological SAE in the registry record), so the harm was compound-specific, as Murata suspected, and does not transfer to the class. The decision-16 dose block is not used: the toxicology never predicted the harm, so it is counted once, here. H4R-knockout haematology was not checked within budget.
safety.note: Two of roughly thirty patients on 300 mg developed agranulocytosis within 6 weeks; the trial stopped; the tox species had shown no haematological signal.
safety.short: Agranulocytosis the tox species never showed
safety.quote: Safety, including adverse events (AE), was comparable between JNJ-39758979 and placebo with the exception of two patients (both receiving JNJ-39758979 300 mg) with serious AE of neutropenia, leading to premature study discontinuation.
